entries.note: baseline snapshot at adoption of skill-provenance/v1
inject shared interaction-policy v1 managed region
add 'Known pitfall: arbitrary gold ordering caps accuracy' section (order policy for structured comparisons; 100%-failure audit signal)
stamp bare `latency` metric unit (ms after SDK 0.22.0, seconds earlier) on the decision ladder (#214)

collapse inline SDK-version stamps into the authoritative docs/version-matrix.md rows with `see version-matrix: <fact_id>` pointers; restamp smart-selector executability to the verified 0.20.1 boundary (Traigent/traigent-skills#221; fact E per #190)
add portable audience, topic, lifecycle-stage, and maturity metadata; instructional body unchanged

a judge inside metric_functions is outside the SDK cost ledger on 0.27.0 (local evaluator settles example cost before metric functions run) so judge spend must be budgeted and capped in user code; the Tier-3 example no longer converts a data-shape exception into an ordinary 0.0 (an objective metric that raises fails the trial closed with EvaluationError); nested explicit metadata object pitfall; new pitfall on scoring what the evaluator is handed (fence strip seam, all-0.0/all-1.0 first paid run is a scorer suspect); claim-scope line that a 0.0 must mean a wrong answer; See Also points at traigent-boost-agent (the bare traigent skill was merged).

review fix: example.metadata is a plain dict - .get() reads None, bracket access raises KeyError (executed on 0.27.0); claim-scope line no longer reads as forbidding the judge template's counted parse-failure 0.0.

rebase PR #288 onto current main and sync interaction-policy v2: recommend next skills only after result-bearing steps or explicit decisions, cap recommendations at three, and attach one eligibility reason per recommendation
Make the Tier 2, Tier 4 and Tier 5 comparators case-insensitive (.strip().lower()) to match the SDK built-in accuracy, so a correct answer in a different letter case no longer scores 0.0.
Point the cost-limit advice at the new cost-metering caveat: on traigent <= 0.27.0 only the first LLM call per row in a custom evaluator is metered.
Emit latency in milliseconds from the Tier 4 custom evaluator and state that a custom_evaluator must put metrics['latency'] on every row, or a latency objective reads 0.0.
Mark Tier 5 (BaseEvaluator subclass) as not wireable through @traigent.optimize on the released SDK and replace its example with a note pointing to Tier 4.
Scope the Tier 5 not-wireable claim to traigent <= 0.27.0 and name the top-level and optimize_sync custom_evaluator paths that accept an instance and then fail at run time.
